title: Evacuation timestamp synchronizer and soft-threshold hedge (hotfix)
author: Maya Patel
description: Background: During a regional overload incident we observed two problematic behaviors: (1) concurrent node-level evacuations in the same cohort sometimes used slightly different evacuation timestamps, which allowed a small window where tenant leases were double-counted for eviction heuristics, causing unnecessary churn; (2) the soft-threshold path that should temporarily relax SLO enforcement while preserving KV prefix cache was too aggressive when combined with speculative prefetch, causing higher tail-latency for critical tenants. This PR introduces a lightweight cross-region evacuation timestamp synchronizer (best-effort, clock-drift tolerant) and a hedging mechanism that gates the soft-threshold relaxation when coordinated prefetch is active. The goal is to reduce false-positive evictions and preserve high-priority tenant latency during transient overloads. What this changes: - Introduces EvacTS protocol: a compact lease-synchronization envelope sent during evacuation orchestration that attaches a monotonic evacuation-id + origin-hash and a micro-timestamp (millis). Implemented as best-effort: nodes will accept and reconcile newer evacuation-ids from upstream controllers; older messages are ignored. This avoids races where two controllers start overlapping evacuations with different epoch anchors. - Adds a soft-threshold hedge: the SLO relaxer now consults a lightweight prefetch-state predicate. If prefetch activity for a tenant exceeds a threshold and eviction pressure is marginal, the relaxer defers full soft-mode and instead applies a graded limit (50%-80% of the intended relaxation) to protect tail latency. - Telemetry: emits evac_ts.accepted, evac_ts.rejected (by-staleness), soft_hedge.applied, and soft_hedge.skipped; updated dashboards with example alert queries included in docs/telemetry/playbooks.md - Backwards compatibility: EvacTS is backward-compatible: older nodes ignore unknown fields; controllers will fall back to existing behavior if no evacuationsync ACKs are observed. - Rollout plan: staged rollout to regional controllers (canary region -> 3 additional regions -> global) with a 1-hour observation window per stage. Fix severity: high (incident-driven hotfix). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for EvacTS reconciliation - [x] Integration test for soft-threshold hedge under simulated prefetch load - [x] Added telemetry and dashboard snippets - [x] Manual canary runs in eu-west-1, eu-central-1 Notes and links: Linear ENG-4482 is the incident follow-up; SUP-1023 tracks a customer-facing symptom. See runbook link: https://linear.redwood.inc/ENG-4482 and dashboard gdoc snippets in docs/telemetry/playbooks.md

release_notes: Hotfix: reduce false-positive tenant evictions by synchronizing evacuation timestamps and add a hedge to soft SLO relaxation when prefetch activity is high. Improves tail-latency stability during regional overloads.
